what_happened.line: The Finance Committee took no formal votes; it heard budget presentations from the Sewer Commission and the school superintendent.
The Sewer Commission presented its budget with a planned step rate increase in FY21, and a possible added cost from a switch to flow metering that is not in the budget.
The school budget was presented as reduced from the original proposal, with the salary reserve cut, alongside COVID costs.
A street light LED conversion was presented, with two options: a Unitil conversion, or a town purchase of the lights using a Green Communities grant.
The town manager was asked to bring street light insurance cost and related information to the next Select Board meeting.

why_it_matters: Sewer rates, school spending and the street light choice each reach residents through a bill or the tax rate, and these were all heard before any vote was taken.
The street light decision sets whether the town pays Unitil or owns the lights, with insurance and upkeep costs still to be answered.
Estimated debt for the new pavement and school project bond was added to the budget, which adds to what the town must pay back.
